You will run two scripts from the repository root, in the Linux/WSL terminal you opened in
[Setup](01-setup.qmd#terminal):

| Script | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `code/01_download_sample.sh` | LSA SAF server + `code/.env` | `data/raw/<PRODUCT>/YYYY/MM/*.nc` |
| `code/02_preprocess_cdo.sh` | raw NetCDF + AOI/YAML bounds | `data/interim/<PRODUCT>/YYYY/MM/*_processed.nc` |

```bash
cd ~/projects/tutorial-repo     # every command on this page runs from here
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Prefer to fill in a form? The [**command builder**](reference.qmd) writes all the commands on this page
for your product, month, AOI and number of CPU cores.
:::

## 1 · Download one month {#download}

### Run it

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Use `code/.env`

Uses `SAMPLE_YEAR`, `SAMPLE_MONTH`, `VARIABLE_NAME` and `URL` from `code/.env`:

```bash
bash code/01_download_sample.sh
```

## Choose the month

Positional arguments **override** `code/.env`: `YYYY MM [PRODUCT] [URL]`.

```bash
bash code/01_download_sample.sh 2015 06 METREF
```

## Another product (FVC)

The product name is used for the output folder; the URL decides what is downloaded.

```bash
bash code/01_download_sample.sh 2015 06 MDFVC \
  "https://datalsasaf.lsasvcs.ipma.pt/PRODUCTS/MSG/MDFVC/NETCDF"
```

## Faster / elsewhere

```bash
JOBS=8 RAW_DIR=/data/lsasaf bash code/01_download_sample.sh 2015 06 METREF
```

:::

**Options**

::: {.flag-table}
| Setting | How to set it | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `YYYY MM` | 1st, 2nd argument | `SAMPLE_YEAR`, `SAMPLE_MONTH` in `.env` | Month to download |
| `PRODUCT` | 3rd argument | `.env VARIABLE_NAME` → `METREF` | Folder name under `data/raw/` |
| `URL` | 4th argument | `.env URL` | Product NetCDF root on the LSA SAF server |
| `JOBS` | environment variable | `4` | Parallel downloads |
| `RAW_DIR` | environment variable | `data/raw` | Where raw files go |
| `ENV_FILE` | environment variable | `./code/.env` | Credentials/settings file |
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
`code/.env` is loaded *after* environment variables, so `URL=… bash code/01_download_sample.sh` is
overwritten by the `URL` line in `.env`. Override the month, product and URL with **arguments**.
:::

### Example output

```text
2015-06: 30 file(s) on server, 30 to download -> …/data/raw/METREF/2015/06
First file: ~6s. Estimated remaining: ~0m44s with 4 parallel jobs
Done: 30 file(s) in 0m52s
```

Re-running is safe: files that already exist are skipped and only failed ones are retried.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Walk through the download script
```{.bash filename="code/01_download_sample.sh (simplified)"}
ENV_FILE="${ENV_FILE:-$PWD/code/.env}"
set -a; . "$ENV_FILE"; set +a                                   # <1>
WGETRC="$(mktemp)"; trap 'rm -f "$WGETRC"' EXIT
printf 'http_user=%s\nhttp_password=%s\n' "$LSASAF_USERNAME" "$LSASAF_PASSWORD" > "$WGETRC"  # <2>

for d in $(seq -w 1 31); do                                      # <3>
  list+=$(wget -q -O- "$SRC/$YEAR/$MONTH/$d/" | grep -E '\.nc$' …)
done

get() { wget -q -O "$f.part" "$1" && mv "$f.part" "$f"; }       # <4>
xargs -P "$JOBS" -I{} bash -c 'get "$1" "$2"' _ {} "$DEST"      # <5>
```
1. Credentials and defaults come from the private `.env`, never from the repository.
2. `wget` reads the password from a temporary file that is deleted on exit — it never appears in the process list.
3. Each day folder of the month is listed; days that do not exist return nothing.
4. Files are written as `.part` and renamed only when complete — an interrupted run never leaves a "finished-looking" half file.
5. `JOBS` downloads run in parallel.
:::

## 2 · Inspect a raw file {#inspect}

Never remap blind. Pick one file and look at variable names, grid and values:

```bash
f=$(ls data/raw/METREF/2015/06/*.nc | head -n1); echo "$f"
cdo -s showname      "$f"   # variable names → MAIN_VARIABLE and QA_VARIABLES
cdo -s sinfo         "$f"   # grid: lon/lat range and step, data type
cdo -s showtimestamp "$f"   # time stamp
cdo -s infon         "$f"   # min / mean / max per variable and number of missing values
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Check yourself
- `showname` lists the product variable (e.g. `METREF`) **and** a QA variable (e.g. `quality_flag`).
- `sinfo` shows a regular `lonlat` grid (for MSG-disk products e.g. `-80 to 80 by 0.05`).
- `infon` shows plausible values for the product (METREF: mm/day, roughly 0–15).
:::

## 3 · Define the region {#region}

The region can come from the YAML bounds **or** from a vector file. Either way the script snaps it
outward to whole raw-grid cells and writes the target grid to `code/preprocess_utils/grid.txt`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Bounding box in YAML

Edit `code/preprocess_utils/config_resolution.yaml`:

```{.yaml filename="code/preprocess_utils/config_resolution.yaml"}
domain:                   # <1>
  lon_min: -17.275
  lon_max: -11.225
  lat_min: 12.225
  lat_max: 16.775
processing:
  parallel: 4             # <2>
  remap_method: bilinear  # <3>
  buffer: 0.2             # <4>
```
1. Degrees (EPSG:4326). Snapped outward to raw cell edges on each run.
2. Files processed at the same time. **This is the only place to set parallelism** for preprocessing — an environment variable `PARALLEL=` is ignored.
3. `bilinear` for continuous fields, `nearest` for categorical ones. Applies to all non-QA variables; QA variables always use nearest neighbour.
4. Extra degrees cropped around the grid, so bilinear interpolation has real neighbours at the AOI edge.

## Vector AOI file

Pass any GeoPandas-readable file (`.shp`, `.gpkg`, `.geojson`, `.parquet`) as the **4th argument**
(or `AOI_FILE=`). Its total bounds become the domain:

```bash
MAIN_VARIABLE=METREF uv run bash code/02_preprocess_cdo.sh \
  0.05 data/raw/METREF data/interim/METREF data/aoi/spatial_units.geosjon
```

:::

::: {.callout-important}
## The script updates the YAML in place
Each run rewrites the `domain:` and `grid:` sections of `config_resolution.yaml` with the **snapped**
bounds (and with the AOI bounds when you pass a vector file). Commit or copy the file if you want to
keep the previous region; restore the repository default with
`git checkout code/preprocess_utils/config_resolution.yaml code/preprocess_utils/grid.txt`.
:::

## 4 · Crop and remap {#preprocess}

### Run it

```bash
export MAIN_VARIABLE=METREF                 # <1>
export QA_VARIABLES=quality_flag            # <2>
uv run bash code/02_preprocess_cdo.sh 0.05 data/raw/METREF data/interim/METREF   # <3>
```
1. **Required.** Must match a name from `cdo showname`; the script stops and lists the available names otherwise.
2. Comma-separated QA/flag variables, remapped with nearest neighbour so flag codes are never averaged. Default `quality_flag`; every name must exist in the file.
3. `uv run` makes `python3` inside the script use the project environment (YAML + grid helper). Arguments: **resolution label** (written to the log — the target grid always follows the raw grid's cell size, 0.05° for MSG, so no false detail is created), **input folder** (searched recursively for `*.nc`) and **output folder** (use one folder **per product** so the cube builder never mixes products).

**All options**

::: {.flag-table}
| Setting | How to set it | Default |
|---|---|---|
| resolution label | 1st argument | YAML `processing.resolution` |
| input folder | 2nd argument | `data/raw` |
| output folder | 3rd argument | `data/interim` |
| AOI vector file | 4th argument or `AOI_FILE=` | none → YAML `domain` |
| `MAIN_VARIABLE` | environment variable | — (required) |
| `QA_VARIABLES` | environment variable | `quality_flag` |
| `CONFIG_FILE` | environment variable | `code/preprocess_utils/config_resolution.yaml` |
| parallel files, remap method, buffer | YAML `processing:` | `4`, `bilinear`, `0.2` |
:::

### Example output

```text
Raw resolution: dx=0.05°, dy=0.05°  (121 x 91 cells)
Aligned bounds: lon -17.275 to -11.225, lat 12.225 to 16.775
Saved updated YAML: …/code/preprocess_utils/config_resolution.yaml
Saved CDO target grid: …/code/preprocess_utils/grid.txt
cdo    remapbil: Bilinear weights from lonlat (129x97) to lonlat (121x91) grid, with source mask (…)
cdo    remapnn: Nearest neighbor weights from lonlat (129x97) to lonlat (121x91) grid
…
Done. Main variables: bilinear; QA variables (quality_flag): nearest-neighbour. Log: data/interim/METREF/cdo.log
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Walk through one file's journey (`process_cdo`)
```{.bash filename="code/02_preprocess_cdo.sh (per file)"}
cdo -sellonlatbox,$CLIP_WEST,$CLIP_EAST,$CLIP_SOUTH,$CLIP_NORTH  in.nc  clip.nc  # <1>
cdo -delname,$QA_CSV  clip.nc  main.nc                                        # <2>
cdo -selname,$QA_CSV  clip.nc  qa.nc
cdo -remapbil,grid.txt  main.nc  main_remap.nc                                 # <3>
cdo -remapnn,grid.txt   qa.nc    qa_remap.nc                                   # <4>
cdo merge main_remap.nc qa_remap.nc merged.nc                                  # <5>
cdo -s sinfo merged.nc && mv merged.nc out.nc.part && mv out.nc.part out_processed.nc  # <6>
```
1. Crop to the target grid **plus the buffer**, so interpolation at the edge has neighbours.
2. Split continuous variables from QA flags.
3. Continuous variables: bilinear (or nearest, from the YAML).
4. Flags: always nearest neighbour — a flag value is a code, not a number to average.
5. Put them back together.
6. Only a readable result is renamed into place; temp files are removed on any failure. Existing valid outputs are skipped, so re-running resumes.
:::

## 5 · Check the output {#check}

```bash
ls data/interim/METREF/2015/06 | head -n3
tail -n 3 data/interim/METREF/cdo.log           # status=processed / failed per file
grep -c "status=processed" data/interim/METREF/cdo.log
f=$(ls data/interim/METREF/2015/06/*_processed.nc | head -n1)
cdo -s sinfo "$f"                                # 121x91 lonlat grid, METREF + quality_flag
cdo -s infon "$f"                                # compare min/mean/max with the raw file
```

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Check yourself
- One `*_processed.nc` per raw file, and no `status=failed` lines in `cdo.log`.
- The grid matches `code/preprocess_utils/grid.txt`.
- Value ranges are close to the raw file's; the number of missing values is plausible (ocean, masks).
:::

### When output is mostly missing

| Likely cause | Check |
|---|---|
| AOI outside product coverage | Compare `sinfo` ranges of raw file and `grid.txt` |
| Wrong variable | `cdo showname` vs `MAIN_VARIABLE` |
| Fill values not decoded | `cdo infon` on the raw file: are huge negative values counted as data? |
| Real masks (sea, clouds, retrieval QA) | Inspect `quality_flag` and the product user manual |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: yaml` / `xarray` | Run the script via `uv run bash …` or `source .venv/bin/activate` |
| `QA variable 'quality_flag' not found` | Set `QA_VARIABLES` to the flag name your product uses (see `showname`) |

## Method notes

- Regridding never adds detail: a finer target grid only interpolates the source.
- Bilinear smooths continuous fields (extremes can shrink); nearest keeps categories but looks blocky.
- Degree cells shrink with latitude (0.05° ≈ 5.5 km at the equator, ≈ 5.3 km at 15° N in longitude).
- Record product version, AOI, grid, remap method and software versions with your results.
